# R6 Gal 6:11–18 — Moo Galatians BECNT
**Range:** 5121–5372
**Lines actually read:** 5121–5367 (body through Additional Notes; trailing blank lines 5368–5372)
**Claim count:** 32

## Claims

### C-R6-001
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo titles 6:11–18 “Closing: Cross and New Creation” and argues that neglecting Pauline letter endings is a mistake nowhere more serious than in Galatians: the ending omits standard features (greetings, travel plans, prayer requests, doxologies) and instead includes a final rebuke of the agitators (vv. 12–13) plus theological comment—crucified to the world (v. 14), new creation (v. 15), “new Israel” (v. 16)—because Galatian urgency leads Paul to cut polite formulas.
- **quote:** "the urgency of the situation in Galatia leads Paul to dispense with some of the usual “polite” formulas"
- **locus:** L5121–L5123
- **passage:** Gal 6:11–18

### C-R6-002
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-creation, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Per Moo (citing B. Longenecker), the ending matches the introduction as eschatological bookends: rescue from the “present evil age” (1:4) is matched by separation from “the world” via cocrucifixion (6:14), and positively by “new creation” (6:15); recognizing participation in this eschatological project should help the Galatians resist agitators bound to a past age already in principle judged.
- **quote:** "both set the situation in Galatia and Paul’s response to it in their appropriate eschatological context"
- **locus:** L5125
- **passage:** Gal 6:14–15; cf. 1:4

### C-R6-003
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, new-creation]
- **claim:** Moo reports Betz’s claim (slight exaggeration) that the ending provides “the hermeneutical key to the intentions of the Apostle”; Paul uses it to sum up his central concern and move readers to action.
- **quote:** "the ending of the letter provides “the hermeneutical key to the intentions of the Apostle”"
- **locus:** L5125
- **passage:** Gal 6:11–18

### C-R6-004
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, circumcision, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo describes a concentric structure: formal frame of Paul’s “signature” (v. 11) and grace wish (v. 18); outer theological antithesis of agitators rebuked (vv. 12–13) matched by plea that such people no longer trouble him (v. 17); center = crucifixion to the world, new creation, and “Israel of God.” Throughout, Weima-noted antitheses: agitators’ selfish motives vs. Paul’s cross-motivation; physical circumcision vs. “marks” of Jesus; this world vs. next; the cross (vv. 12, 14) creates the antitheses.
- **quote:** "The structure of the passage is concentric."
- **locus:** L5127
- **passage:** Gal 6:11–18

### C-R6-005
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** On 6:11, Moo holds that Paul opens with an “autograph”: readers should notice “such large letters” written “in my own hand.” The aorist ἔγραψα with reference to letters denotes the physical act of writing down, not general authorship; though Chrysostom thought Paul wrote all of Galatians by hand, Moo with the vast majority takes ἔγραψα as an epistolary aorist referring only to 6:11–18, after an amanuensis (cf. Rom 16:22; 2 Thess 3:17; Philem 19).
- **quote:** "what Paul himself “wrote down” is only 6:11–18"
- **locus:** L5133
- **passage:** Gal 6:11

### C-R6-006
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On why the letters are large, Moo lists three scholarly suggestions—(1) unskilled handwriting (Deissmann); (2) failing eyesight, linking 4:13–15 (Witherington; du Toit); (3) emphasis like bold font (majority)—and concludes we cannot know why the letters are large, though option 3 is viable and Witherington rightly asks why Paul does not highlight large letters elsewhere for emphasis.
- **quote:** "At the end of the speculation, we cannot know why the letters here are large."
- **locus:** L5135
- **passage:** Gal 6:11

### C-R6-007
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** In 6:12–13 Moo says Paul focuses on two points about the agitators: (1) agenda/failings—trying to force circumcision, wanting the Galatians circumcised, not themselves keeping the law; (2) motives—good showing in the flesh, avoiding persecution because of Christ’s cross, boasting in the Galatians’ flesh. Concern with “flesh” brackets the verses (Martyn); σάρξ has physical connotation (circumcision context) with possible theological nuance of human weakness/sin from 5:13–26 / 6:7–8 (sarcasm: bragging in flesh reveals enslavement to the un-Spiritual).
- **quote:** "The agitators’ concern with “flesh” thus brackets these verses"
- **locus:** L5137
- **passage:** Gal 6:12–13

### C-R6-008
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Paul identifies agitators allusively (“as many as,” ὅσοι) as wanting to “make a good showing” (εὐπροσωπῆσαι)—rare verb, “good + face,” mere outward appearance; they try to force circumcision (conative present ἀναγκάζουσιν). Moo links ἀναγκάζω to 2:3–4 (false brothers compelling Titus) and 2:14 (Peter forcing Gentiles to live like Jews): in all three, Jews pressure Gentiles toward circumcision/torah authority.
- **quote:** "In all three of the situations, Jews are putting pressure on Gentiles to be circumcised"
- **locus:** L5139
- **passage:** Gal 6:12; cf. 2:3–4, 2:14

### C-R6-009
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo notes a biblical-theological case could be made for agitators’ circumcision/torah insistence, but Paul here ignores their theological rationale (treated in 2:15–4:7) for personal polemic: purpose is to avoid persecution “because of the cross of Christ” (dative likely causal). On μόνον, Moo prefers Lightfoot’s qualifying link over NIV/BDAG “solely,” so Paul is not claiming quite so strongly that avoidance of persecution is their only reason.
- **quote:** "Paul is not claiming quite so strongly that the only reason the agitators are insisting on circumcision is to avoid persecution."
- **locus:** L5141
- **passage:** Gal 6:12

### C-R6-010
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Insisting on circumcision would avoid persecution because proclaiming Messiah without requiring converts to be circumcised and follow the law would draw Jewish criticism, ostracism, or physical punishment; Jewett’s Zealot-pressure context and the Antioch crisis (2:11–14) illustrate. Per Dunn, persecution would come not for preaching the cross alone but for preaching it as Paul understood it—as the sole basis for acceptance with God.
- **quote:** "it was for preaching the cross of Christ as Paul understood it, as the sole basis for acceptance with God"
- **locus:** L5143
- **passage:** Gal 6:12

### C-R6-011
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** On (οἱ) περιτεμνόμενοι in 6:13, present tense could mean people “being circumcised” (Gentile converts or Gentile agitators—Munck/Schoeps), but Moo with most scholars rejects process-sense and Gentile-agitator views as misfitting context and letter evidence; the present stresses the fact of circumcision: “the circumcised” / circumcision party (NRSV; R. Longenecker).
- **quote:** "to understand the participle as stressing not the process of “being circumcised” but the fact of circumcision"
- **locus:** L5145
- **passage:** Gal 6:13

### C-R6-012
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** On agitators “not themselves keep[ing] the law,” Moo surveys options (distance from Jerusalem/sacrificial laws; non-rigorous practice; failing to keep law’s ultimate Christ-pointing meaning) and prefers reading via Rom 2: Jews fail to “do” the law they pride in possessing—OT/NT critique (Acts 7:53)—so accepting circumcision obliges one to do “the whole law” (3:10; 5:3) which they cannot fulfill; the agitators exhibit this problem.
- **quote:** "accepting circumcision puts people under an obligation—to do “the whole law”—that they are unable to fulfill."
- **locus:** L5147
- **passage:** Gal 6:13; cf. 3:10; 5:3

### C-R6-013
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** In 6:13b agitators want the Galatians circumcised “so that they might boast in your flesh”: σάρξ is primarily the physical flesh cut in circumcision; Hays: rivals “want to display the foreskins of the Galatians as trophies of their own triumphant persuasive power,” with possible theological irony of allying with the old-age power of flesh.
- **quote:** "want to display the foreskins of the Galatians as trophies of their own triumphant persuasive power"
- **locus:** L5149
- **passage:** Gal 6:13

### C-R6-014
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** In 6:14 adversative δέ and fronted ἐμοί mark stark contrast: Paul boasts only in “the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” (optative μὴ γένοιτο with καυχᾶσθαι). His passion for the cross’s centrality/exclusivity appears elsewhere in Galatians (2:18–21; 5:11) and famously 1 Cor 2:1–5; remarks are not narrowly autobiographical but exemplary. For ancients, boasting in crucifixion would be bizarre (shameful violent death; Hengel)—like boasting in guillotine/electric chair—but the singular event of Christ’s crucifixion, where God was reconciling the world (2 Cor 5:19), transforms the cross.
- **quote:** "May it never boast in anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ"
- **locus:** L5151
- **passage:** Gal 6:14

### C-R6-015
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-creation, paul-apostle, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Relative οὗ refers to the cross (not Christ): “to me the world has been crucified, and I to the world”—decisive separation and wholly new relationship (cf. 5:24 crucified the flesh). Parallel 2:19–20 (died to law; crucified with Christ). κόσμος here is apocalyptically colored spatiotemporal realm of sin/death/evil (like 1:4 “present evil age”), not neutral cosmos. Per Betz, boasting rests on what happened through Christ to me; cocrucifixion frees believers from the world’s baneful influence and allegiance; cross is “the transformative event that ended the old order of things” (Hays).
- **quote:** "Paul’s crucifixion means a decisive separation between the world and himself"
- **locus:** L5153
- **passage:** Gal 6:14; cf. 2:19–20; 1:4

### C-R6-016
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, new-creation, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Verse 15 (γάρ) rephrases v. 14: negative half elaborates “world”; “new creation” describes what replaces it. “Neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything” echoes a Pauline slogan (Gal 5:6; 1 Cor 7:19) dismissing worldly valuations; Paul associates even God’s old-covenant circumcision requirement with the worldly system judged by Christ’s death/resurrection; adding uncircumcision broadens to all purely worldly significance (cf. 3:28 Jew/Gentile, slave/free, male/female)—ethnicity, class, gender distinctions no longer matter (Martyn).
- **quote:** "neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything… but the new creation"
- **locus:** L5155–L5161
- **passage:** Gal 6:15; cf. 5:6; 3:28

### C-R6-017
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-creation, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** καινὴ κτίσις is compact; only other Pauline use is 2 Cor 5:17. κτίσις can mean “creature” or “creation.” Some take individual renewal (Hubbard; Lightfoot; Burton; R. Longenecker); some community focus; but most (Vos; Stuhlmacher; Hoch; Jackson; Dunn; Hays) take “new creation” as the new state of affairs Christ’s death and resurrection inaugurated.
- **quote:** "most interpreters think “new creation” refers generally to the new state of affairs that Christ’s death and resurrection has inaugurated"
- **locus:** L5163
- **passage:** Gal 6:15

### C-R6-018
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-creation, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Phrase “new creation” never occurs in OT but equivalents appear in Jewish texts (Jub. 1.29; 4.26; 1 En. 72.1; 1QS 4.25; 2 Bar. 44.12). Adams: established technical term in Jewish apocalypticism for transformed creation after world destruction/renewal. Wider background: Isaiah 40–55 re-creation after exile and “new heavens and earth” (Isa 65:17–22; 66:22–24); personal focus in Jeremiah/Ezekiel new heart; Joseph and Aseneth conversion language; rabbinic inner renewal—yet overall background favors cosmic/apocalyptic sense.
- **quote:** "“the expression ‘new creation’ was an established, technical term in Jewish apocalypticism"”
- **locus:** L5165
- **passage:** Gal 6:15

### C-R6-019
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-creation, holy-spirit, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Context confirms cosmic reading: “new creation” contrasts “world” (v. 14) and “present evil age” (1:4). Theodoret: strictly the transformation after resurrection of the dead, but NT eschatology inaugurates it in Christ’s death/resurrection. Foundations: individual conversion and new Jew-Gentile community (3:28; Eph 2:11–22), but the term is wider—entire transforming work with cosmic reverberations (Moo 2006; 2010a). Paul contrasts agitators’ modest “newness” with sweeping newness from Christ’s death/resurrection.
- **quote:** "embracing the entire transforming work of God, a work that will ultimately have cosmic reverberations"
- **locus:** L5167
- **passage:** Gal 6:15; cf. 1:4

### C-R6-020
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, justification]
- **claim:** Galatians’ ending is distinctive among Pauline peace-promises by pairing “peace” and “mercy” (no other concluding promise mentions mercy) and making the promise conditional—only for those “who follow this rule.” As Paul cannot include usual thanksgiving in the introduction, he cannot promise unqualified peace; the letter stands between conditional curse 1:8–9 and conditional blessing 6:16 (Betz; Hays) because the situation is too dire and Galatian response too uncertain.
- **quote:** "the entire letter stands between the conditional curse of 1:8–9 and the conditional blessing of 6:16"
- **locus:** L5169
- **passage:** Gal 6:16; cf. 1:8–9

### C-R6-021
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-creation, holy-spirit, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** V. 16 is effectively exhortation: join those who experience peace and mercy by following “this rule” (κανών = rod/standard; later “canon”). τούτῳ may refer to whole of v. 15 (Betz; R. Longenecker) but more likely “new creation” (v. 15b; Bruce; Kwon)—incorporating Spirit, faith, and love (5:6) otherwise unmentioned in the ending. Confirmed by στοιχέω, used in 5:25 of keeping in step with the Spirit: indicative/imperative linkage—new creation carries its own values (Spirit, faith, love) vs. old age values (flesh, circumcision, law).
- **quote:** "it is more likely that the “rule” has to do with “new creation” in verse 15b"
- **locus:** L5171
- **passage:** Gal 6:16; cf. 5:25; 5:6

### C-R6-022
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** “Peace” (εἰρήνη) is a key new-covenant blessing, often with grace in salutations (Gal 1:3); more often objective reconciliation with God and others (Rom 5:1; Eph 2:15–17) rooted in OT šālôm hope than subjective well-being. “Mercy” (ἔλεος) is rare in Paul (nine other occurrences). Pairing and order peace-then-mercy are unusual versus other NT pairings where ἔλεος comes first (natural progression: mercy creates peace).
- **quote:** "in the four other NT passages where they are found together, ἔλεος comes first"
- **locus:** L5173
- **passage:** Gal 6:16

### C-R6-023
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Striking word order separates εἰρήνη and ἔλεος by a prepositional phrase (εἰρήνη ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς καὶ ἔλεος). αὐτούς antecedent = “as many as follow this rule.” Syntactical options for “Israel of God”: (1a) epexegetic καί—identical to those who follow the rule (NIV); (1b) conjunctive καί—separate/overlapping group (ESV); (2) peace on rule-followers, mercy also on Israel of God (HCSB). These decisions impinge on the identity of “the Israel of God.”
- **quote:** "the controversial issue of what Paul means by “the Israel of God”"
- **locus:** L5175–L5187
- **passage:** Gal 6:16

### C-R6-024
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, justification]
- **claim:** Option 1a (epexegetic) yields “Israel of God” = new-covenant people (Christians/faithful Christians)—the most common interpretation (Köstenberger; Dahl; Chrysostom; Calvin; Luther; Lightfoot; Barclay; Martyn; Schreiner; Beale; Hays; R. Longenecker; et al.). Options 1b/2 suggest a distinct Jewish group: (1) Israel as a whole; (2) Jewish Christians; (3) Israel destined for salvation (Rom 11:26); (4) combination of 2+3.
- **quote:** "“Israel of God” would then refer to the new-covenant people of God. This is, in fact, the most common interpretation"
- **locus:** L5189–L5191
- **passage:** Gal 6:16

### C-R6-025
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Evaluating options, Moo finds syntax favors 1b or 2: epexegetic καί is possible (Turner; BDAG; Acts 5:21 Sanhedrin/gerousia as Köstenberger cites) but not usual; word-order symmetry and peace-mercy sequence might suggest two blessings on two entities. Still, the hanging-nominative condition with αὐτούς is unusual and could have produced awkward word order, so identification remains possible.
- **quote:** "Syntax favors either view 1b or 2."
- **locus:** L5193–L5203
- **passage:** Gal 6:16

### C-R6-026
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** On usage: Richardson argued “Israel” for the church only from Justin (~AD 160) and always ethnic in the NT. Moo notes disputed Rom 9:6b and 11:26; he himself takes both as ethnic Israel (Moo 1996) so they shed no certain light. Preponderant NT usage suggests ethnic Israel, yet Rom 9:6 (any view) distinguishes some spiritual “Israel,” and 1 Cor 10:18 “Israel according to the flesh” implies “Israel according to the Spirit”—Spirit creating a people beyond ethnic boundaries.
- **quote:** "1 Cor. 10:18, where Paul’s reference to “Israel according to the flesh” (AT) implies the existence of an “Israel according to the Spirit.”"
- **locus:** L5205
- **passage:** Gal 6:16

### C-R6-027
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, justification, circumcision]
- **claim:** Context of Galatians is decisive for Moo’s 1a identification: throughout, old Jew/Gentile barriers, circumcision, and law are removed; in Christ no Jew/Greek distinction (3:28); seed of Abraham = all who believe (3:7–29); Gentiles “like Isaac, children of promise” (4:28). It is “inconceivable” that Paul would reerect ethnic blessing on an Israel distinct from Christian believers. Though data do not all point one way, this context point decides: “Israel of God” (only here in NT) tacitly recognizes ethnic/national Israel but insists the Israel that counts before God is constituted on different grounds—coextensive with all who follow the rule (including believing Gentiles).
- **quote:** "we think this last point is decisive in favoring interpretation 1a above: “the Israel of God” is another way of referring to “all who follow this rule.”"
- **locus:** L5207–L5209
- **passage:** Gal 6:16

### C-R6-028
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-creation, moo-galatians-becnt, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Summary of 14–16 controlling vision: believers (1) removed from this world’s controlling influence; (2) participate in new creation, God’s ultimately cosmic restoration; (3) belong to God’s people redefined around Jesus the Messiah—everything reconstituted in light of the cross; live out of this world-changing reality (v. 16a).
- **quote:** "Everything, Paul is saying, has been reconstituted in light of the cross"
- **locus:** L5211
- **passage:** Gal 6:14–16

### C-R6-029
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** In 6:17 Paul returns to agitator concern; unlike v. 14, reference is only to himself (personal toll; cf. 4:12–20; 5:12). τοῦ λοιποῦ more likely temporal “from now on” than mere “finally.” Third-person imperative addresses agitators: “Let no one cause me trouble.” Implicitly, if Galatians stop paying attention, agitators will not trouble Paul.
- **quote:** "But they will not “trouble” Paul if Christians for whom he feels spiritual responsibility, such as the Galatians, stop paying attention to them."
- **locus:** L5213
- **passage:** Gal 6:17

### C-R6-030
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, circumcision, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Ground (γάρ): “I bear the marks of Jesus on my body” (στίγματα). Word elsewhere only Song 1:11; ancient use for slave brands and religious tattoos. Explicit “body” = physical marks. Moo prefers scars from persecution for Christ (cf. 2 Cor 4:10) over deliberate loyalty mark; may signal dedication to God and/or slave of the Lord—overlapping. Physical scars contrast the physical mark of circumcision; Eastman paraphrase: identity markers = scars branded for Jesus—“Become like me!”
- **quote:** "Paul probably intends these physical scars to stand in contrast to the physical mark of circumcision."
- **locus:** L5215
- **passage:** Gal 6:17

### C-R6-031
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** 6:18 is a standard Pauline grace wish (all letters), circling back to the formal focus of v. 11. Grace defined as of “the Lord Jesus Christ” (genitive hard to categorize). “With your spirit” only elsewhere in 2 Tim 4:22. Unique among concluding grace wishes: “brothers and sisters” (ἀδελφοί)—perhaps emphasizing Gentile Galatians with Jewish believers as one spiritual family. Per Martyn, blessings 6:16 and 6:18 and Amen show they have been dealing fundamentally with God, not simply with Paul.
- **quote:** "Perhaps Paul has added it to emphasize one last time that the Gentile Galatian believers, along with Jewish believers such as Paul, belong to one spiritual family."
- **locus:** L5217–L5219
- **passage:** Gal 6:18

### C-R6-032
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Additional Notes compare standard Pauline closing elements: Galatians lacks travel plans, prayer requests, associates, mutual greetings, holy kiss, greetings from associates, and doxology; it does include autograph (6:11), warning/exhortation (6:12–15, 17), eschatological wish/promise (6:16), prayer-wish for peace (6:16), and concluding grace (6:18). Textual notes: 6:12 subjunctive διώκωνται preferred over indicative; no Ἰησοῦ after Χριστοῦ; 6:13 present περιτεμνόμενοι preferred as more difficult; 6:15 no “in Christ Jesus” assimilation to 5:6; 6:16 future στοιχήσουσιν best supported; 6:17 Ἰησοῦ preferred for τὰ στίγματα τοῦ.
- **quote:** "the ending of Galatians stands out by virtue of the number of common elements not found here"
- **locus:** L5221–L5367
- **passage:** Gal 6:11–18

## Coverage summary
- **Read in full:** Section V intro (neglected endings; eschatological bookends with 1:4; concentric structure; agitator/Paul antitheses); Moo’s translation 6:11–18; exegesis 6:11 (autograph/large letters/amanuensis); 6:12–13 (agitators’ agenda, flesh bracketing, force circumcision, persecution motive, Zealot/Jewish pressure, περιτεμνόμενοι as circumcision party, law-keeping critique via whole-law inability, boast in flesh as trophies); 6:14 (boast only in cross; world crucified / I to world; parallel 2:19–20; apocalyptic κόσμος); 6:15 (neither circumcision nor uncircumcision; Pauline slogan; new creation—cosmic not merely individual; Jewish apocalyptic + Isaiah background; inaugurated eschatology); 6:16 (conditional peace+mercy; κανών = new creation; στοιχέω/Spirit link; peace/mercy semantics; syntax options 1a/1b/2; “Israel of God” crux—Moo decides for epexegetic 1a = all who follow the rule / new-covenant people, context decisive over syntax/usage); summary vision 14–16; 6:17 (trouble; stigmata as persecution scars vs. circumcision); 6:18 (grace wish + adelphoi); Additional Notes table of closing elements + textual variants 6:12–17.
- **Not present / thin:** No extended treatment of unrelated chapters; apparatus is textual notes only, not full MS collations. Moo’s identification of “Israel of God” is explicit and argued at length (critical crux expected).
- **Gaps vs expected brief:** All expected loci covered (6:11 large hand; 6:12–13 motives; 6:14 cross/world; 6:15 new creation; 6:16 Israel of God; 6:17 marks; 6:18 grace; concentric structure; 1:4 bookends).
